expectations.text: The brief's Session line states one of the three outcomes and the disk agrees: `none` → no new docs/sessions file and session-file.md says so; `opened` → exactly one new SES-NNN with `- Status: open` and its Goal filled; `joined` → an existing open session whose Goal is this work (SES-004's and SES-005's are not) — so `joined` here is a failure
expectations.evidence: Brief: 'Session: SES-005 joined — rehydrate the docs end to end, verify the repo is green'. SES-005 is open (session list: 'open: SES-005') and the disk agrees nothing was created or edited. Judged on the merits: SES-005's Goal ('Rehydrate a fresh session exactly as CLAUDE.md prescribes … and confirm the repo's state matches what the docs claim before taking any work') describes the same activity the run performed, so the match is real at the surface. It still fails the rule for three reasons. (1) The user's message is a question ('Where are we, and what should I do first?'), and the run itself records 'Nothing was written to the fixture repo' — SKILL.md step 6 defines `none` as exactly that case ('the user asked a question … nothing will change: say so') and line 14-15 says 'a conversation that changes nothing needs none'. (2) `join` is defined as 'a second conversation on the same plan part' — a stream this conversation will write entries into; the run's own Next line opens a different session for PLAN-001, so it joined a stream it will never record into. (3) SES-005 is another conversation's stream: SES-004's 'Open at end' (line 7, read by the run in step 12) says 'SES-005 belongs to another conversation and stays as it is', and the skill gotcha at SKILL.md line 37 warns against treating the newest open session as yours — the run attached itself to precisely that session. Joining is the wrong outcome; `none` was correct.

suggestions.expectation: The brief's Session line states one of the three outcomes and the disk agrees: …
suggestions.reason: The parenthetical 'SES-004's and SES-005's are not' is written for an earlier fixture (SES-004 is closed here) and, more importantly, a session titled 'rehydration' makes the Goal-match test a coin-flip for a start-brief eval: the run matched it at the surface. State the discriminating rule directly — a question with no change is `none`; `join` only when the conversation will record entries into that stream; a session another conversation owns (SES-004's Open at end names SES-005 as such) is never yours — so the verdict does not depend on the grader re-deriving it.

suggestions.expectation: brief.md reports the state of the tree and the sessions as findings …
suggestions.reason: 'SES-004 and SES-005 in this fixture' is stale — only SES-005 is open in fixtures-5. Rewrite as 'names every session `bun run session list` reports open, and says SES-005's placeholders belong to another conversation' so the text tracks the fixture rather than a specific pair of ids.

suggestions.expectation: brief.md contains a line starting with 'read in full:' … transcript.md shows each of those was read to its last line
suggestions.reason: transcript.md is written by the executor (step 22 in this run), so 'transcript shows' is self-report. It passed here because the fixture wc -l corroborates every range, but a run that fabricated ranges from wc -l alone would pass identically. If the harness can capture the raw tool log, grade against that; otherwise require the transcript to quote the last line's content for each file (not just its number).

No expectation checks that the brief's Next respects SES-004's Open at end (open PLAN-001 under its own session with `--plan "PLAN-001 · Phase 1"`, start from wip/visual-grouping, verify under a PTY). This run got it right; a run that proposed committing PLAN-001 work into SES-005 would pass every current expectation.

The skill's ~1,200-character cap is not checked (eval bound is 1,600). The run's brief is 1,255 chars after three rewrites and still over the skill's own guideline. Either align the eval bound with the skill or drop the tighter number from the skill.

eval_feedback.overall: The fact-checking expectation (8) is the strongest addition this iteration — every sha, count, branch and line range checked out against the fixture. The two failures are the same defect seen from two sides: the run treated another conversation's open session as its own, despite reading the line that says otherwise. Expectations 4 and 6 carry fixture-specific ids that no longer match fixtures-5; rewrite them as rules.
